approach: Add `run/format.rs` with `format_work_tree(dir, changed_paths, ctx)`. It is Athena code, not an agent command. If `dir/Cargo.toml` exists and a changed path is a non-deleted `*.rs`, it runs `cargo fmt --all` and then `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both go through the existing `crate::checks::run_check`, so they get the timeout, the kill switch, redaction and output capture. It returns `Skipped(reason)`, `Done` (the tree passes `--check`) or `Unfixed{output,note}` (the check still fails, for example a parse error). `producer_loop` calls it once after the `loop`, when a report has ended it, and before `Ok(Flow::Go(..))`. It skips a pinned study (`ctx.pin_dir`) and says so. The call builds the environment with `athena_agent::env::build(Side::Produce)` (the same call the checks use) and takes the timeout from `budget.check_timeout_s`. It prints a `format` UI line when the tree changed (tree id before and after) or when the result is Unfixed. `candidate_stage` and `build_candidate` read `snapshot.change_list()` afterwards, so the candidate commit, the checks and the verifier all see the formatted tree. An Unfixed result changes no flow: the configured `fmt` check fails on the same tree and reports the same error in its output tail. Tests drive the real `cargo fmt` on temp crates, and one end-to-end fake-driver job runs the repository's own `cargo fmt --all --check` as its check.

decisions.choice: Call the format step once at the end of producer_loop (after the `loop`, before `Ok(Flow::Go(Reported{..}))`), not after each pass.
decisions.reason: This is what the accepted reading says and what criterion 3 greps for. The candidate (candidate.rs:34), the checks and the verifier all read the tree after the loop, so one call covers them. The send-back checks inside the loop (scope, decision gate, mirror drift) see the producer's own edits. rustfmt changes layout only, and only in files the producer already changed when the base is fmt-clean.

rejected.option: Format after every producer invocation, before `change_list()` at producer.rs:339
rejected.why: The loop's send-back checks would then see formatted content, but this departs from the reading and criterion 3, runs the formatter several times, and gains nothing when the base is clean.
It splits the producer stage across two files and leaves the timed-out and Stop paths ambiguous. At the end of `producer_loop` the Stop returns have already left.

decisions.choice: Run both commands through `crate::checks::run_check` with `CheckSpec{run: ["cargo","fmt","--all"], kind: Command}` and the `--check` form. The environment comes from `athena_agent::env::build(Side::Produce)` and the timeout from `budget.check_timeout_s`.
decisions.reason: It reuses tested code (checks.rs:513-638) for timeout, process-group kill, kill switch, registry, redaction and the failure tail (`failure_section`). The Unfixed output is then the same shape as the failed-check output the fmt check records, which is what criterion 2 compares. The same env path as the checks (mod.rs:1937-1948) means cargo and rustup resolve the same way.

rejected.why: `run_bounded` discards output, so criterion 2's output text would be lost, and it has no kill switch or redaction.

rejected.option: Use the producer's spec.env with the CargoShim
rejected.why: The shim takes a build slot for cargo build, test, clippy and check. fmt builds nothing, and a slot wait would hold the job for no reason.

decisions.choice: Skip unless the work tree has `Cargo.toml` and the change list holds a non-deleted `.rs` path. Also skip for a pinned study (`ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`).
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for Cargo.toml. The `.rs` condition keeps a docs-only or Cargo.toml-only job from rewriting pre-existing unformatted Rust files outside its scope. A pinned study mounts a checkout inside the work tree (producer.rs:147-149) that the formatter must not touch. Existing fake-job tests have no Cargo.toml, and the one that does (tests.rs:4185) leaves its Rust file clean.

rejected.why: A job that changed no Rust could have its diff grow by base layout drift and then fail the scope check in check_and_verify (mod.rs:1843-1862).

decisions.choice: An Unfixed result changes no flow: log one UI line and leave the tree as it is.
decisions.reason: The reading says unfixable errors stay and the normal fmt check reports them. A second reporting path would duplicate the gate and could relax it. Out of scope: relaxing the fmt gate.

rejected.option: Send the producer back with the rustfmt error
rejected.why: It adds a send-back class (send_back.rs text builders and tests) beyond one focused step. A separate request can add it.

rejected.option: Fail the job at the step
rejected.why: It would duplicate the fmt check and bypass the baseline pre-existing comparison (`mark_pre_existing`).

decisions.reason: The step is host code spawning a process, not a Bash command through the hook, so the deny of `cargo fmt` without `--check` (policy.rs:682) still binds the roles. Criterion 5 and Out of scope both need this.

rejected.option: Allow `cargo fmt` for the producer role
rejected.why: Listed out of scope, and it would move the guarantee from mechanism back to prose.

decisions.choice: Put the new tests inside `produce_and_verify_order_tests` in run/tests.rs, reusing its helpers.
decisions.reason: `athena_with`, `repo`, `commit_file`, `base_script`, `Lines` and `finished_job` are private to that module, and `format.rs` items are `pub(super)`, visible to `run::tests`. The module has a fake driver whose `FakeTurn.edits` write files into the producer snapshot.

rejected.why: The deliverable list names tests.rs, and the helpers for the end-to-end test live there.

files.purpose: `Formatted` outcome enum and `format_work_tree(dir, changed, ctx)`. It checks the Cargo.toml and changed-`.rs` guards, runs `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, both through `checks::run_check`. It returns Skipped, Done or Unfixed{output, note}.
Add `mod format;` next to the other stage modules (lines 61-68). Nothing else changes.

After the `loop` in `producer_loop` and before `Ok(Flow::Go(..))`, build the env, take `snapshot.change_list()`, call `format::format_work_tree` (skip when `ctx.pin_dir` is set), compare tree ids before and after, and print a `format` UI line. Extend the doc comment with the new stage and its root cause.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/run/format.rs. Define `pub(super) enum Formatted { Skipped(&'static str), Done, Unfixed { output: String, note: Option<String> } }` and `pub(super) fn format_work_tree(dir: &Path, changed: &[(char, String)] or &[DiffEntry-derived paths], ctx: &CheckContext<'_>) -> Result<Formatted>`. Return Skipped when `dir/Cargo.toml` is not a file, or when no changed path ends in `.rs` with a status other than D. Otherwise run `run_check` on a `CheckSpec{name:"format", run:["cargo","fmt","--all"], kind: Command, skip_when_only: None}` and ignore its pass or fail (a parse error exits non-zero). Then run `run_check` on `["cargo","fmt","--all","--check"]`. If it passed, return Done. If not, return Unfixed with the check's `output_tail` and `note`. Add module docs with the root cause: a layout-only defect rejected jobs, and agent roles may not run `cargo fmt` without `--check` (policy.rs:682).
In crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs add `mod format;` among the module declarations (lines 61-68).

In producer.rs, after the `let report = loop { .. };` block and before `Ok(Flow::Go(Reported { .. }))`, add a block. Skip when `ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`. Otherwise: build `env` with `athena_agent::env::build(&EnvSpec{agents:&jc.config.agents, job:id.as_str(), job_dir:&self.state.job_dir(&id), snapshot:snapshot.dir(), side:Side::Produce, capability_env:&capability_env}, |k| std::env::var(k).ok()).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?`. Build a `CheckContext{dir: snapshot.dir(), env:&env, timeout: Duration::from_secs(jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s), registry:&self.state.registry(), job:id.as_str(), redactor: ctx.redactor}`. Take `before = snapshot.work_tree_tree()?` and `changes = snapshot.change_list()?`. Call `format::format_work_tree`. Print `format     cargo fmt rewrote the work tree before the checks` if `work_tree_tree()` differs afterwards. Print `format     cargo fmt --check still fails: <first line>; the fmt check will report it` for Unfixed. Extend the `producer_loop` doc comment with this stage.

Write the CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## [Unreleased]` stating the outcome and the root cause (a job whose only defect is rustfmt layout reaches the verifier formatted; an unfixable error still fails the fmt check; agent policy unchanged).

In run/tests.rs add to `produce_and_verify_order_tests`: a `FMT_CHECK` const; a helper that builds a temp crate and a `CheckContext`; and the tests of criteria 1, 2, 5 (unit tests on `format_work_tree` against real cargo fmt) and 3 and 4 (one end-to-end test: `commit_file` Cargo.toml and a clean src/lib.rs, a script wrapper that sets the producer turn's edits for README.md and a mis-formatted src/lib.rs, `athena_with(.., FMT_CHECK, ..)`, `go`, then assert Landed, the candidate's changes and `show_file` equality, and a `format` UI line).

Run `cargo fmt --all` yourself, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` (include `cargo test -p athena-core`, `-p athena-agent`, and `-p athena-cli --test lifecycle --test retry --test drain --test mirrors`). Confirm `git status` shows only the five deliverables.

No refusal or matching rule is added or changed, so no `refusal_corpus` case is mapped. Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` anyway as a regression guard; this plan cites no corpus case ids because it read none and relies on none.

risks.risk: The base is not fmt-clean, or a producer's change touches files the base left unformatted. `cargo fmt --all` would then rewrite files the producer never touched and could add paths outside the job's allowed paths.
risks.mitigation: The step runs only when a `.rs` file is already in the change list, and the scope check in `check_and_verify` (mod.rs:1843-1862) still names any file outside scope. The reading accepts the base-clean assumption. The risk is also listed in the changelog bullet.

risks.risk: `cargo fmt` needs cargo, rustfmt and, with rust-toolchain.toml, rustup resolution, under a cleared environment.
risks.mitigation: The environment comes from `env::build`, the same `env_pass` lists the checks use, and the tests pass PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME through. If the tool cannot start, `run_check` records a failed run with a note; the step returns Unfixed and the job proceeds to the fmt check, which fails the same way as today.

risks.risk: The step runs real cargo in unit tests, so they need rustfmt installed and take a few seconds.
risks.mitigation: CI runs `cargo fmt --check`, so rustfmt is present; the tests use tiny crates with no dependencies. A missing rustfmt makes the tests fail rather than skip, as the behavior-evidence default requires.

risks.risk: A pinned study mounts a checkout inside the work tree; formatting it would alter pinned files.
risks.mitigation: The call is skipped when `ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`, with a Skipped reason; no pinned job has a changed `.rs` of its own to format.

risks.risk: The step runs on a nested run too (`self.nested`).
risks.mitigation: The format step is idempotent and cheap, and a nested producer's tree is formatted the same way. The outer job's scope check sees the combined change as before.

risks.risk: `rustfmt` output varies by toolchain version, so the expected text in test 1 could drift.
risks.mitigation: The test uses simple constructs whose layout is stable (a long array and `fn f( )->u32{1}`) and compares with the formatted result of the same toolchain via the post `--check` pass, plus a literal for the simple function body.

demonstrations.method: Test `a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes` in run/tests.rs. It writes a temp crate (Cargo.toml and src/lib.rs with `pub const LONG: ...` crammed on one line and `fn f( )->u32{1}`). It builds a `CheckContext` (env: PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME from the process; `Registry::new(tempdir)`; `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`). It first runs `run_check` with `cargo fmt --all --check` and asserts the check fails, which shows the defect. Then it calls `format_work_tree(dir, &["src/lib.rs".into()], &ctx)`. It asserts the outcome is `Done`, that the file text equals the expected rustfmt layout, and that `run_check` of `cargo fmt --all --check` now passes.
demonstrations.observes: The file bytes change to the formatted layout, the outcome is Done, and the fmt check goes from failed to passed. Also run `cargo test -p athena-core` as a whole.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the formatter run, the file stays mis-formatted, so the content assertion and the post `--check` assertion both fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `run::format::format_work_tree` (added by plan step 1), called with a real `CheckContext` over a tempdir and the real `cargo fmt`. No double is used. The `run_check` pre- and post-check comes from checks.rs:513 (exists).

demonstrations.method: Test `an_unfixable_fmt_error_is_reported_and_the_fmt_check_fails_with_the_same_text`. The temp crate's src/lib.rs is `pub fn broken( {` (a parse error). It calls `format_work_tree`, asserts the outcome is `Unfixed{output,..}` and that `output` holds a line starting with `error` and the file name `lib.rs`. It then runs `run_check` with the configured fmt spec (`cargo fmt --all --check`) on the same dir. It asserts `!passed` and that the check's `output_tail` contains that first `error` line from the step's output. It also asserts the broken file is byte-identical afterwards, since nothing was fixed or relaxed.
demonstrations.observes: A failed fmt result whose rustfmt error text appears in the failed check's output tail. The tree is not changed and the gate is not relaxed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step swallowed the failure and returned Done, the Unfixed assertion fails. If it rewrote or deleted the broken file, the byte-identity assertion fails. If the check's output tail did not carry the error, the contains assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: The same production entry point `format_work_tree` plus `crate::checks::run_check`, with the real cargo and rustfmt in a tempdir. No double. The seam is added by step 1 and the test by step 5.
